requirement:
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.

The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate for every obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`. I did not read implementation source. The assessment rests on the supplied test text.

Obligations and the tests that cover them, all in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]`:

- **80% file threshold on exact counts.**
  - `fn[exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions]` asserts `threshold(79_999,100_000)` is false (a rounded 80.0% still fails), `threshold(80_000,100_000)` is true, and `threshold(0,0)` is false.
  - The same test checks that 4/5 passes at exactly 80%.
  - It also checks that another file's higher percentage cannot rescue `driver.rs`, which fails at 0/1 and at 7/10.
- **Not an average of file percentages.** The 100% file and the 70% file average 85%. The test asserts the report still fails.
- **No 80% target within each function.** `fn[a_function_below_eighty_percent_needs_no_exception_when_its_file_passes]` has a function at 1/3 inside a file at 10/12. It asserts the report passes with no accepted exceptions. `fn[exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions]` also asserts no function failure is reported for an executed function in a file at 70%.
- **Union across processes.** `fn[children_and_filtered_runs_contribute_to_the_same_union]` checks two processes that cover disjoint lines, one a child. The union gives 5/5. A later all-zero run does not erase that coverage.
- **Freshness, selection and the active build.**
  - `fn[inactive_and_stale_measurements_cannot_raise_the_file_total]` covers an inactive build's success, which cannot raise the total.
  - It covers a stale success beside a fresh failure, which is excluded and reported as stale.
  - It covers a run whose build configuration is not the active one, which makes the check fail.
  - `fn[stale_missing_legacy_and_invalid_store_cannot_use_older_success]` covers missing, legacy, stale and corrupt store cases, none of which can reuse an older success.
- **Exception evidence.** `fn[accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution]` and `fn[missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report]` check that a file below the threshold passes only with a current accepted exception. They check that missing, rejected and stale reviews leave it failing. `fn[function_explanations_never_transfer_to_other_functions_or_the_file]` checks that a function exception does not transfer to the file or to other functions.
- **Unmeasured executable file.** In `fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]`, a file with executable code but no measurements reports `not measured — FAIL`, not a percentage. `fn[accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution]` shows that same file passes only with an accepted exception, again with no fabricated percentage.
- **No executable obligations.** The same test uses a struct plus a trait declaration. It asserts `code.rs: no executable obligations — pass`, with no exception needed. `fn[default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not]` checks the inventory flag in both directions. Declaration-only code and a derive-only struct are treated as having no obligations. A macro invocation and a default trait body are not.
- **Missing lines alone do not mean no obligations.** `fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]` has `fn missing(){}` with no recorded lines. It is reported as not measured and failing, not as having no obligations. The macro case in `fn[default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not]` supports this.
- **Parse failures stay visible.** `fn[measured_file_threshold_remains_checked_when_source_parsing_fails]` and `fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]` assert that a parse failure is reported and that a measured file's threshold is still checked. The parsing requirement itself is cited context and was not reassessed.

I found no gaps. Every test cited here already carries a `{test}` reference to the subject.

execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the

child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception

Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file

:::{req} rust_item_coverage.parsing
Repository validation parses every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs`
file among the sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root
`vendor` directory. It reports a Rust parse failure rather than silently
skipping the file.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} index.summary
Saved execution-coverage checks compute line coverage from the union of
instrumented file-and-line locations in the eligible current results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, including child processes.
Each location counts once in the denominator and is covered when any selected
process has a positive execution count. Percentages use these union counts,
rather than averaging process reports.
When the current set has no usable instrumented lines, or any current result
has unavailable measurements under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`, combined coverage is
reported as unavailable. The check does not publish measured coverage
percentages or threshold results computed from only the remaining readable
results. Otherwise, absent file or function measurements remain subject to
their coverage obligations.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
